The Pilten district 'eventually fell to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth' (no dates) and is probably outside the outline; the page does not settle it.

region.text: Courland and Semigallia, with Mitau as the new capital

ledger.note: 1561: Gotthard Kettler becomes the first Duke of Courland. 'In 1561, during the Livonian Wars, the Livonian Confederation was dismantled and the Livonian Order was disbanded'; under the Treaty of Vilnius (28 November 1561) the north went to Lithuania and 'Gotthard Kettler, the last Master of the Livonian Order, became the first duke of Courland'; the duke is a vassal of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (to 1569) and then of Poland-Lithuania.

region.text: the duchy, whose duke the Swedes captured

ledger.note: 1658: Sweden holds Courland. 'The Swedish army captured Duke Jacob (1658-1660)' in the Swedish-Polish war of 1655-1660; the page does not describe the extent of the occupation.
1660: the Treaty of Oliwa ends the Swedish hold. 'Courland regained Tobago on the basis of the treaty and held it until 1689'; the page does not say when the Swedes left the duchy itself.

24 October 1795: the Duchy of Courland is incorporated into the Russian Empire. 'With the signing of the final document on 24 October 1795, the Duchy of Courland was incorporated into the Russian Empire'; the table ends Peter von Biron's reign on 28 March 1795, also the Third Partition date in the infobox.
24 October 1795: the last duchy ends and the Courland Viceroyalty follows, a governorate from 1796 (Courland Governorate page).

notes:
Cliopatria's row 'Duchy of Courland' covers only 1734-1793; the duchy lasted from 1561 (Gotthard Kettler, Treaty of Vilnius 28 November 1561) to 1795 (incorporation signed 24 October 1795). The dossier therefore adds two keyframes (1561-1733, 1794-1795) that repeat the 1734 and 1793 outlines. Cliopatria's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth shape covers the Courland cells in 1575-1705 and nothing covers them in 1706-1733, and the Russian Empire shape covers them from 1794: the compiler should draw the duchy as a vassal of the Commonwealth (a Grand Duchy of Lithuania vassal in 1561-1569, per the page) rather than twice.
The vassal relation is the suzerain's to record: the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth dossier (eu-15) and the grand-duchy-of-lithuania dossier need vassal_start events for duchy-of-courland in 1561 and 1569 and a vassal_end in 1795. The page also says '1569: made part of the Crown of the Polish Kingdom' and '1726: incorporated into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth' without saying what changed on the ground. The page does not mention the Second Partition (1793), the Landtag of 17 March 1795 or an exact abdication date for Peter von Biron; the dates 28 March and 24 October 1795 are the page's.
Pilten (Piltene): 'it fell to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth' (no dates) and the governorate 'united the lands of the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia and the District of Pilten' in 1795, so Pilten is outside the duchy until its end and the Russian Empire's gain; whether Cliopatria's 28,201 km2 shape includes it is not settled (the shape and the gazetteer's Courland region differ by about 23 cells).
Rulers are read from the page's table; it lists no duke between Louis Ernest (27 June-6 December 1741) and Charles (from 10 November 1758). Maurice of Saxony, 'elected duke in 1726, but only managed to maintain himself by force of arms till the next year', is not in the strip. Goldingen (Kuldiga) was the residence of Duke Wilhelm in the western part after the 1596 division, not a capital.
Not reached within the page budget (2 pages): the 1772 one-cell change, the Pilten boundary, the Commonwealth's Swedish wars after 1629. Area check: infobox 27,290 km2 (no year) against 28,201 km2 for 1734: ratio 1.03.
